scientific_name: Physiological disorder caused by calcium deficiency in fruit tissues
description: Blossom-end rot is a physiological disorder caused by a lack of calcium in developing fruits. It affects rapidly growing fruits when calcium supply to fruit tissue is insufficient. The disorder leads to tissue collapse at the blossom end of the fruit and can cause significant yield losses.
symptoms: Small light green or yellow spot at the blossom end of the fruit
Sunken dark brown or black lesion on fruit tip
Fruit tissue collapse and dry rot
Secondary bacterial soft rot in severe cases
favorable_conditions: Low calcium availability in plant tissues
Poor root development or root damage
High temperature and rapid fruit growth
spread: Not infectious; it is a physiological disorder
Occurs when calcium transport to fruits is insufficient
Often triggered by water stress or nutrient imbalance
management: Maintain consistent soil moisture with proper irrigation
Improve soil structure for better root growth
Use mulching to regulate soil moisture and temperature
Monitor soil nutrient levels with soil testing
biological_control: Use beneficial microbes such as Bacillus subtilis to improve plant health
Apply Trichoderma species to support root growth and nutrient uptake
Use organic soil amendments like compost to improve soil structure
prevention: Ensure adequate calcium levels in soil
Use drip irrigation to stabilize water supply
Avoid root damage from cultivation or diseases
source: Principles of Plant Nutrition – Mengel & Kirkby
Plant pathology and vegetable crop management literature
